why: fallacious (based on faulty reasoning) is a near-opposite of irrefutable
'justify' means to show something is right, not to make it accepted or legal; not a true synonym
propriety (polite, proper behavior) is a near-opposite of insolence (ant: politeness, respect)

cloze.s: At the board meeting, many parents were quick to ___ the school's decision to cancel art classes, calling it a terrible mistake.

why: original context did not signal criticism; 'scrutinize' could also fill it
abdicate (give up a position) is a near-opposite of wrest (take by force); ant list has surrender/yield
stupendous (amazing) is a near-opposite of prosaic (ant: extraordinary, exciting)
nonchalant (calm and relaxed) is an opposite of frenzied (ant: calm, relaxed)
derision (mocking someone as worthless) overlaps with condescension's synonym disdain; could be picked as closest in meaning
confound's def includes 'surprise someone'; overlaps with startle in the meaning/closest-meaning questions

set.note: Comes from the “notice or measure” sense of appreciate, not the “be thankful” sense.

why: 'Not related to' appreciate is misleading: the words share a root; the difference is only of sense
'over' alone is not a recognizable synonym of afresh
'agony' matches the old 'violent pangs' sense, not the taught 'in the throes of (a difficult process)' sense
'mawkishness' is rarer than the headword; learners at this level would not recognize it
despondent (very unhappy, hopeless) is a near-opposite of jovial (ant: gloomy, grumpy)
paucity (having very little) is a near-opposite of affluence (ant: poverty, want)
whittle (reduce gradually) overlaps with abate (become less); could be picked as closest in meaning
apocryphal (believed but probably not true) overlaps with fallacious's synonyms false/mistaken
'head' and 'elder' are not true synonyms of matriarch (no gender, no family-leader sense)
'profanity' today chiefly means swearing, not disrespect for something sacred
'paradox' contradicts the item's own note; 'contradiction' alone is broader than a phrase joining opposites
fittingly (in a way that is right for the situation) overlaps with deservedly/rightly and could fill the cloze
'amply honored' could plausibly fill the cloze

set.def: of weather: bad and unpleasant, with rain, snow, strong wind, or cold

why: inclement weather need not be cold (e.g., summer thunderstorms); old def required cold
rejuvenate (restore energy) is a near-opposite of deplete (ant: replenish, restore)
